notes: Sealed held-out briefs for scripts/run_baseline_gate.py. Written by an independent agent on 2026-10-04 and not read by the maintainer while tuning the skill. Open them only for a release decision; once a run on these briefs has informed a change, write a new sealed set.

briefs.prompt: Design the home screen a child sees in a family chores app, showing which jobs are theirs today and how much pocket money they have earned this week.
Design the screen for a single field in our Android app for crop farmers. A farmer standing at the edge of it wants to know what was last done there and what needs doing next.
Design the live walk screen for our iOS dog-walking app. An owner at work opens it to check where their dog is and how the walk is going.
Our ski resort's app needs a screen that tells skiers which lifts and runs are open right now and how long the lift queues are. Could you design it?

Map the flow in our home insurance app (iOS and Android) for a customer whose kitchen has been flooded by a burst pipe, from opening the app to seeing their claim number and knowing when someone will be in touch.
Map the flow for a trip in a car-sharing app, from reserving a nearby car to locking it at the end and seeing the final price. The app is on iOS and Android.

Write a UI spec for the CPR guidance screen of a first-aid app. Whoever is using it has never done this before, is kneeling over someone who has collapsed, and has laid the phone on the floor so that both hands are free for chest compressions.
Create a UI spec for the file browser and file preview screens of a cloud storage app on Android tablets and foldables.

We need a UI spec for the defect-logging screen in our iPad app for construction site inspectors. An inspector walks through a half-finished building with the iPad resting on one forearm, wearing work gloves and often in poor light, photographs each defect and pins it to the floor plan before moving on.

Write a UI spec for the recording screen of our iPhone interview-recording app for journalists. The phone lies on a table between the reporter and the person being interviewed, and the reporter looks down only to check that it is still recording or to mark a moment worth coming back to.

Review this donation screen in our charity's iOS app for usability and accessibility. From top to bottom: a full-width photo with the appeal's title over it in white 13 pt text; four amount chips (5, 10, 25 and 50 euros), each 28 pt tall, with 25 already selected; a 'Give monthly' switch that is on by default; card number, expiry date and security code fields whose only labels are grey placeholder text; and a 'Donate' button that does not say how much will be charged. A mistyped card number turns the field's border red and nothing else changes. No screenshot is available.

Could you review the 'My shifts' screen in our Android shift-scheduling app for supermarket staff for usability and accessibility? The week is seven columns, each 40dp wide and headed by a single letter. A shift is a coloured block in its column - green for confirmed, amber for a pending swap, red for changed by a manager - with the start and end times in white 10sp text and no other label. Offering a shift for a swap means long-pressing its block, which nothing on the screen mentions. Tapping a block opens a pop-up with the department and break time, which closes by itself after three seconds. The week's total hours are at the very bottom in light grey 11sp text. No screenshot is available.

Create a typography and spacing system for a calendar app on iOS and Android that has a month grid with up to three event titles inside each day cell and a day view laid out as an hour-by-hour timeline.

Create a typography and spacing system for our Bible reading app on Android phones and tablets. A chapter is long running text with verse numbers set into it, section headings, footnotes and cross-references, and on a tablet two translations can be read in parallel columns.

Write the design rationale and developer handoff notes for the redesigned home screen in our mobile carrier app (iOS and Android). The new design: the data left this month is a large figure at the top, with the renewal date under it; minutes and texts are two smaller figures in one row below; an 'Add data' button sits under that row; the latest bill is a card showing the amount and the due date; and the old usage graph is removed - daily usage now opens on its own screen when you tap the data figure.

Please prepare the design rationale and developer handoff for the redesigned 'New expense' screen in our expense claims app. It now opens straight into the camera, so an employee photographs the receipt first; the amount, date and merchant read from the photo then appear as three editable fields above a row of category chips, and 'Submit' is pinned to the bottom. Mileage claims used to be a separate tab and are now reached from a 'No receipt?' link under the shutter button. The project code used to be typed in every time and now defaults to the last one used, shown in a single row that opens a picker. We removed the currency converter and the notes field.
